name: Foursquare Open Source Places (fsq-os-places)
what_it_holds: Foursquare's open global POI dataset: 100M+ POIs, 200+ countries/territories, 1000+ place categories (Foursquare's taxonomy includes a 'Hotel'/'Lodging' branch), 20+ core attributes (name, address, lat/lon, category, chain flags). Hosted on Foursquare's own site / HuggingFace / cloud storage (Parquet), refreshed periodically (monthly-ish cadence per Foursquare's public statements); no dedicated GitHub data repo found (searched fsq-os-places / foursquare-os-places, both 404), so treat GitHub only as a discovery pointer to the external host.
why_useful: A second independent global hotel/lodging POI census (cross-check against Overture places) with a documented 'Hotel' category, letting the team build/validate a hotel-count-by-city supply series and check counts against known chain unit disclosures.
time_coverage: periodic full-dataset refreshes, no long history of vintages published
size_hint: 100M+ POIs total (lodging category a small subset)
license: Foursquare open data licence (check terms; free for commercial+non-commercial per their announcement)
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
why_all: A second independent global hotel/lodging POI census (cross-check against Overture places) with a documented 'Hotel' category, letting the team build/validate a hotel-count-by-city supply series and check counts against known chain unit disclosures.

name: whosonfirst-data (org, e.g. whosonfirst-data-venue-us-ca)
what_it_holds: Mapzen-originated open gazetteer, 823+ per-country/state git repos of GeoJSON 'venue' records (a placetype that includes hotels), sourced partly via a historical Foursquare data partnership. Example: whosonfirst-data-venue-us-ca (691 commits) holds California venue GeoJSON records. Because every record edit is a git commit, the commit history itself is a de facto point-in-time log of when a venue (hotel) appeared/closed/moved — unusual for POI data.
why_useful: A git-versioned historical venue gazetteer that plausibly includes US/global hotels going back to ~2015-2017 is a genuine point-in-time hotel-POI source (gap #4 + #8 combined), unlike Overture/Foursquare which only publish current snapshots.
geography: global, split by country then US by state
time_coverage: ~2015-2017 onward per commit history; project itself looks dormant (mapzen.com is defunct) with the newest visible activity as late as Aug 2026 in some repos, so still receiving occasional automated updates
size_hint: 823+ repos; per-state venue repo sizes not confirmed, likely thousands of records each
license: check LICENSE.md per repo (historically CC0-ish for WOF admin data; venue data licence terms vary by contributor)
last_activity: mixed; some repos updated as recently as Aug 2026, overall project largely dormant since Mapzen's 2017 shutdown
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
why_all: A git-versioned historical venue gazetteer that plausibly includes US/global hotels going back to ~2015-2017 is a genuine point-in-time hotel-POI source (gap #4 + #8 combined), unlike Overture/Foursquare which only publish current snapshots.

name: hrecht/censusapi
what_it_holds: R package (186 stars, CRAN + GitHub) giving lightweight access to 1,500+ US Census Bureau API endpoints via `getCensus()`/`listCensusApis()`/`listCensusMetadata()`. Endpoint list is generic (ACS, SAIPE, SAHIE, international trade, economic time series) but because it hits Census's full API catalog by URL/dataset code, it can reach County Business Patterns (CBP) and Quarterly Services Survey/Services Annual Survey endpoints (NAICS 721 accommodation establishment counts, employment, receipts) even though the README doesn't name CBP/QSS explicitly.
why_useful: A ready client for pulling NAICS 721 (accommodation) establishment counts/employment/payroll by county from Census CBP/QSS/SAS — exactly the 'lodging census' tooling the theme asks for — without hand-rolling Census API calls.
time_coverage: whatever vintages Census publishes for CBP (annual, ~2-year lag) / QSS (quarterly)
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
why_all: A ready client for pulling NAICS 721 (accommodation) establishment counts/employment/payroll by county from Census CBP/QSS/SAS — exactly the 'lodging census' tooling the theme asks for — without hand-rolling Census API calls.

Broadest-coverage Census client found (1,500+ endpoints beyond just ACS), useful if the team wants Census Bureau series beyond ACS (e.g. Business Formation Statistics, Household Pulse Survey) for consumer-strength or housing-supply proxies.

name: Ontario-Hotel-Performance-Analysis
what_it_holds: Monthly Occupancy %, ADR, and RevPAR for hotels across Ontario, Canada regions/cities (Greater Toronto Area, North Western Ontario, etc.), Feb 2023-Dec 2025, sourced from the Ontario Open Data Portal (originally separate monthly Excel sheets, cleaned into a Power BI model). Repo holds a Datasets folder, a Hotel Performance Report.pbix, and a PDF report. MIT licensed.
why_useful: A real government-sourced, regional hotel RevPAR/ADR/occupancy series for a non-US market (Canada) at sub-national geography, which is more granular than the MAR/HLT RevPAR-from-releases we already hold and touches gap #8 (hotel supply/demand, regional RevPAR) and gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, Canada StatCan-adjacent). Read-across to short-term-rental competition and Canadian travel demand for ABNB.
size_hint: Unspecified row count; monthly panel across multiple Ontario regions/cities over ~3 years (small, tens to low hundreds of rows)
last_activity: not confirmed exactly; recent (2026 based on data coverage through Dec 2025)
duplicate_of_holding: Extends but does not duplicate the MAR/HLT RevPAR-from-releases we hold (that is company-level, this is Canadian regional/government-sourced)
themes: Hotel chain and REIT public datasets: loyalty program sizes, unit counts, Marriott/Hilton/Hyatt pipelines, hotel REIT portfolio RevPAR by market from filings
why_all: A real government-sourced, regional hotel RevPAR/ADR/occupancy series for a non-US market (Canada) at sub-national geography, which is more granular than the MAR/HLT RevPAR-from-releases we already hold and touches gap #8 (hotel supply/demand, regional RevPAR) and gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, Canada StatCan-adjacent). Read-across to short-term-rental competition and Canadian travel demand for ABNB.

name: tx-hotel-heatmap
what_it_holds: TypeScript pipeline (scripts/build-data.ts) that parses Texas Comptroller hotel-occupancy-tax filings (data/hotels.csv: taxpayer, location, room count, reported revenue) at the INDIVIDUAL HOTEL level, plus data/periods/ holding per-period Comptroller files across multiple quarters, computing trailing-12-month RevPAR (revenue / rooms / 365) and ADR/occupancy per property; outputs a geocoded GeoJSON (public/hotels.geojson) bucketed by RevPAR percentile for a Next.js/Mapbox heatmap. Texas-only, county/city granularity via geocoding, updated 2026-07-22.
why_useful: Fills gap #8 (state-level hotel occupancy/lodging-tax data, individual-property RevPAR) with a real government administrative source (Texas Comptroller occupancy tax) at finer-than-market granularity, and demonstrates a repeatable pull/parse method that could be adapted to other states (Nevada, Florida bed tax) named explicitly in the same gap.
time_coverage: Multiple historical quarterly/monthly Comptroller filing periods through ~2026 (exact start year not stated in README excerpt)
size_hint: One CSV of TX hotel filings + a periods/ directory of historical per-period files; individual-hotel row grain, likely thousands of properties statewide
duplicate_of_holding: Distinct from held Hawaii DBEDT / municipal STR registries and California TOT panel — this is Texas hotel (not STR) occupancy-tax data with property-level RevPAR, which we do not currently hold for Texas
themes: Booking-curve / pace / pickup datasets for hotels and STRs (on-the-books, forward bookings), Key Data / Transparent / Lighthouse (OTA Insight) samples, revenue-management forward curves
why_all: Fills gap #8 (state-level hotel occupancy/lodging-tax data, individual-property RevPAR) with a real government administrative source (Texas Comptroller occupancy tax) at finer-than-market granularity, and demonstrates a repeatable pull/parse method that could be adapted to other states (Nevada, Florida bed tax) named explicitly in the same gap.
